I have experienced this first hand. I had a middle eastern guy on a project who was tasked with building a computer model of a building that was to be subjected to seismic loads in order to measure the behavior of the structure. He made the model, and when I ran the analysis, nothing came out right. I had a rough estimate of what to expect based on prior analyses, but what I got defined my expectations completely. It wasn't until I actually looked at the model that I discovered that the guy hadn't bothered to confirm the correct orientation of the columns (I-beams) so everything was facing the same direction.

If you're not familiar with structural design, section shape determines the flexural behavior of the element in question, which I shaped cross sections are singly symmetric, so have two different section behaviors depending on the axis which load is being applied on.

This meant that, since the guy put the columns in the wrong way, the structural system wasn't behaving as intended for analysis, and would have been insufficient in design, simply because the guy lacked the critical thinking ability to check the most basic of things.
